Rashi on Nazir 28b:10:1.hebrew: לא נהנין ולא מועלין - כדאמר מר: חטאות המתות ודמי חטאת ההולכין לים המלח, בכולן לא נהנין ולא מועלין. לא נהנין — מדרבנן, ולא מועלין — משום דלאו בני הקרבה נינהו:
Rashi on Nazir 28b:10:1.english: One may not benefit, and [the law of] misuse does not apply - As the Master said: Sin-offerings that are left to die, and the money for a sin-offering that is taken to the Dead Sea — with regard to all of them, one may not benefit, and [the law of] misuse does not apply. "One may not benefit" — by rabbinic law; and "[the law of] misuse does not apply" — because they are not fit for sacrifice.

Rashi on Nazir 28b:11:1.hebrew: הלכה היא בנזיר - שהאיש מזיר, ולא האשה:
Rashi on Nazir 28b:11:1.english: It is a halakha with regard to a nazirite - That a man can make [his son] a nazirite, but a woman cannot.

Rashi on Nazir 28b:1:1.hebrew: ולתנא דידן - כיון דאיזדריק עלה אחד מן הדמים, לאלתר אשתריא בחמרא, ולית לה ניוול. וכיון דלית לה ניוול, אינו יכול לומר: אי אפשי באשה מנוולת:
Rashi on Nazir 28b:1:1.english: And according to our tanna - Once one of the bloods [of her offerings] has been sprinkled on her behalf, she is immediately permitted [to drink] wine, and she suffers no disfigurement. And since she suffers no disfigurement, he cannot say: “I do not want a disfigured wife.”

Rashi on Nazir 28b:1:2.hebrew: אינו יכול להפר משום בזיון קדשים - דהואיל ואין הבעלים מתכפרים בו, אין הבשר נאכל:
Rashi on Nazir 28b:1:2.english: He cannot nullify [the vow] due to the degradation of consecrated [offerings] - For since the owner does not achieve atonement through it, the meat may not be eaten.

Rashi on Nazir 28b:2:1.hebrew: מתקיף לה ר' זירא אמאי - הוי בזיון קדשים? לזרוק דמן שלא לשמן, ויתיר בשר באכילה בזריקת דם שלא לשמן:
Rashi on Nazir 28b:2:1.english: Rabbi Zeira objects to this: Why - [Why] is there a degradation of consecrated items? Let [the priest] sprinkle their blood not for their own sake, and permit the meat to be eaten by sprinkling the blood not for their own sake.

Rashi on Nazir 28b:2:2.english: Is it not taught: The blood shall be sprinkled - [Namely,] not for their sake.

Rashi on Nazir 28b:3:1.hebrew: ואם היתה שבת לא יזרק - לפי שאין הבשר נאכל בשבת, שאין צליית קדשים דוחה את השבת:
Rashi on Nazir 28b:3:1.english: And if it was Shabbat, [the blood] shall not be sprinkled - Because the meat cannot be eaten on Shabbat, as the roasting of consecrated [meat] does not override Shabbat.

Rashi on Nazir 28b:3:2.english: And if he sprinkled, [the offering] is accepted - Provided that he burns the sacrificial parts in the evening.

Rashi on Nazir 28b:4:1.hebrew: אי דשחט עולה ושלמים - ברישא — ה"נ, דאפשר למיהוי להו תקנתא בזריקה. אלא הכי קאמינא לך: כגון דשחט חטאת ברישא, דאי מיפר לה בעל — תו לא הוי ליה תקנתא, דה"ל כחטאת שנתכפרו בעליה:
Rashi on Nazir 28b:4:1.english: If he slaughtered a burnt-offering and peace-offering - [If he did so] first, indeed so, as it is possible for them to have a remedy through sprinkling [the blood]. Rather, this is what I am saying to you: [It is a case] where he slaughtered the sin-offering first, for if the husband nullifies [her vow], it no longer has a remedy, for it is considered like a sin-offering whose owners have achieved atonement.

Rashi on Nazir 28b:5:1.hebrew: ומנא תימרא דכל מאי דבעי שחיט ברישא כדתנן - אם גילח על אחת משלשתן, יצא:
Rashi on Nazir 28b:5:1.english: And from where do you say that whichever [offering] he wishes he may slaughter first? As we learned: - If he shaved after one of the three of them, he has fulfilled [his obligation].

Rashi on Nazir 28b:6:1.hebrew: בד"א - כיון דנזרק עליה אחד מן הדמים אינו יכול להפר — בתגלחת טהרה, הואיל ושותה יין בו ביום, וכדאמרן:
Rashi on Nazir 28b:6:1.english: In what case is this said - [That] once one of the bloods has been sprinkled on her behalf, he cannot nullify [her vow — this applies] to a shaving of purity, since she drinks wine on that very day, and as we said.

Rashi on Nazir 28b:6:2.hebrew: אבל בתגלחת טומאה - אע"פ שנזרק עליה אחד מן הדמים, יפר. ר"מ אומר: אפי' בתגלחת טהרה כו':
Rashi on Nazir 28b:6:2.english: However, with regard to a shaving of impurity - Even though one of the bloods [of her offerings] has been sprinkled for her, he may nullify [her vow]. [The mishna continues:] “Rabbi Meir says: Even at a shaving of purity, etc.”

Rashi on Nazir 28b:7:1.hebrew: ות"ק אמר לך - משום תגלחת לא אפשר להפר, דלא הויא עליה מנוולת משום תגלחת, דאפשר לה בפאה נכרית, ומיחזיא כאינה מגלחת:
Rashi on Nazir 28b:7:1.english: And the first tanna [could have] said to you - On account of shaving, it is not possible [for him] to nullify [the vow], as she is not disfigured to him on account of shaving, for it is possible for her [to wear] a wig, and she appears as though she is not shaven.

Rashi on Nazir 28b:7:2.hebrew: ור' מאיר סבר בפאה נכרית איידי דזוהמא - דאית לה, לא ניחא ליה. ולכך יכול להפר לה, לפי שיכול לומר: אי אפשי באשה מגולחת:
Rashi on Nazir 28b:7:2.english: And Rabbi Meir holds: [Regarding] a wig, since [it has] dirt - That it has [dirt], he is not pleased with it. And therefore, he can nullify [the vow] for her, because he can say: “I do not want a shaven wife.”

Rashi on Nazir 28b:8:1.hebrew: גילח - בתוך ימי נזירותו, או שגילחוהו קרוביו בתוך ימי נזירותו, או שמיחה הבן תוך ימי נזירותו, ואפילו ביום אחרון:
Rashi on Nazir 28b:8:1.english: [If] he shaved - Within the days of his naziriteship; or his relatives shaved him within the days of his naziriteship; or the son objected within the days of his naziriteship, and even on the last day.

Rashi on Nazir 28b:8:2.hebrew: או שמיחוהו קרוביו - הרי זה בטלה נזירותו, ודמי חטאת ילכו לים המלח:
Rashi on Nazir 28b:8:2.english: Or his relatives objected to him - Behold, his naziriteship is canceled, and the money for the sin-offering shall go to the Dead Sea.

Tosafot on Nazir 28b:11:1.hebrew: גמ'. אשה לא - דקתני: "אין האשה מדרת בנה בנזיר":
Tosafot on Nazir 28b:11:1.english: Gemara: "A woman cannot" - For it taught [in the Mishnah]: "A woman cannot vow that her son should be a nazirite."

Tosafot on Nazir 28b:11:2.english: "A halakha" - [Transmitted] to Moses from Sinai with regard to a nazirite.

Tosafot on Nazir 28b:1:1.hebrew: משום הפסד קדשים - שאם יפר לה קודם זריקה, ושוב אינה צריכה לקרבנות הללו, ואסור לזרוק דם. ופריך: אמאי איכא הפסד? יפר לה, ולזרוק דמו שלא לשמו, ויותר הבשר באכילה מן הזבחים שנזבחו שלא לשמן — דכיון דהיפר לה ואינה עוד נזירה, שוב אין עומדין לשמן, ואפילו יזרוק דמן סתם כשרין, דסתמא [שלא] לשמן קיימי. וה"ק: יזרק דמו, דסתמא שלא לשמן קיימי, אלא לשם שלמי נדבה, כיון דאינה עוד נזירה:
Tosafot on Nazir 28b:1:1.english: "Due to the loss of consecrated property" - For if he nullifies [the vow] for her before the sprinkling [of the blood], she no longer needs these offerings, and it is forbidden to sprinkle the blood. And [the Gemara] objects: Why is there a loss? Let him nullify [the vow] for her, and let [the priest] sprinkle its blood not for its sake, and the meat will be permitted for eating, [just as with] sacrifices that were slaughtered not for their sake — for since he nullified [the vow] for her and she is no longer a nazirite, they no longer stand for their [original] purpose, and even if he sprinkles their blood without specification they are valid, because by default they stand [not] for their [original] purpose. And this is what [the Gemara] means: Let its blood be sprinkled, for by default they stand not for their [original] purpose, but rather for the sake of a voluntary peace-offering, since she is no longer a nazirite.

Tosafot on Nazir 28b:2:1.hebrew: כבשי עצרת ששחטן - שלא לשם עצרת, או ששחטן לפני עצרת — בערב עצרת, או לאחר עצרת — הדם יזרק ביו"ט עצמו. וקאי ארישא: שלא לשמן — (או) לשם שלמי נדבה — וע"י כן הותר הבשר באכילה; דאי לית ליה נדרים ונדבות קרבין ביו"ט, א"כ לא יקטיר אימורים עד הערב, ולא יאכל הבשר עד הערב, [דכל כמה] דלא מיקטרי אימורין, בשר לא מישתרי באכילה. ומ"מ, כי נמי אין נדרים ונדבות קרבין ביו"ט, מותר לזרוק הדם. ואם היתה שבת — לא יזרוק, דהוי כמו תיקונו מדרבנן, ואסור. אלמא, [מותר] לזרוק הדם שלא לשמן. וא"ת: אמאי לא מייתי מתני' (לעיל נזיר דף כד.): "עולה תקרב עולה, ושלמים יקרבו לשלמים"? וי"ל: דלא דמי; דהתם, בשעת שחיטה היפר לה, ובין בזריקה ובין בשחיטה עומד שלא לשמן. אבל הכא, דבשעת שחיטה היה עומד לשמן, ועתה בשעת זריקה עומד שלא לשמן — לא מיתכשר שלא לשמן. וצ"ל: דלהך כבשי עצרת נמי לא דמי; דהתם, לא נשחטו לשמן, אבל הכא, כיון דנשחטו לשמן — [שמא] כיון דנשחטו לשמן, דלא מכשרי שלא לשמן? דבפ' התכלת (מנחות דף מז:) מיבעיא להש"ס: הא כבשים ששחטן לשמן ואבד הלחם, מהו שנזרוק דמן של כבשים שלא לשמן, כו'? וא"כ, הא דקאמר "יזרוק", מיירי שנשחטו שלא לשמן! וצ"ל: דלא דמי; דהתם, כבשים מעיקרא בשחיטת זבח, ועיקר הזבח בלחם מתכשר, הילכך כי אבד לחם נמצא הזבח מיפסיל והוי כמו אבד. אבל הכא, כיון דסתמא כשר כמו לשמן, כדאמר בריש זבחים (דף ב:), השתא נמי דשחטן לשמן, ומשום תקנה נעשה כאילו נעשה סתמא לענין להתיר לזרוק דמן. [אי דשחט עולה או שלמים, הכי נמי לר"ע דליכא הפסד]; אלא, [הב"ע] דשחט חטאת [ברישא], דאין לו תקנה לזרוק שלא לשמן, דחטאת מיפסל שלא לשמן לשום שלמי נדבה, דחטאת אינו בא נדבה:
Tosafot on Nazir 28b:2:1.english: The sheep of Atzeret that one slaughtered - [This means one slaughtered them] not for the sake of Atzeret, or that one slaughtered them before Atzeret — on the eve of Atzeret — or after Atzeret. "The blood shall be sprinkled" [means] on Yom Tov itself. And [this ruling] refers to the first clause: [where they were slaughtered] not for their sake, [or] for the sake of voluntary peace-offerings, and thereby the meat became permitted to be eaten. For if [the tanna] does not hold that vows and voluntary offerings may be sacrificed on Yom Tov, if so, he may not burn the sacrificial portions [on the altar] until the evening, and the meat may not be eaten until the evening, [since as long as] the sacrificial portions are not burned, the meat is not permitted for consumption. And nevertheless, even if vows and voluntary offerings are not sacrificed on Yom Tov, it is permitted to sprinkle the blood. And if it was Shabbat, he may not sprinkle [it], as it is like [an act of] repairing it by rabbinic law, and is [therefore] prohibited. Thus [it is seen that it is permitted] to sprinkle the blood not for its own sake. And if you say: Why does [the Gemara] not bring [as proof] the mishna (above, Nazir 24a): "The burnt-offering shall be offered as a burnt-offering, and the peace-offering shall be offered as a peace-offering"? And one can say: It is not comparable. For there, at the time of slaughter he [had already] nullified [the vow] for her, so both at sprinkling and at slaughter it stands [to be offered] not for its [original] sake. But here, where at the time of slaughter it stood [to be offered] for its sake, and now at the time of sprinkling it stands [to be offered] not for its sake, it is not validated not for its sake. And one must say: But neither is it comparable to these sheep of Atzeret! For there, they were not slaughtered for their sake; but here, since they were slaughtered for their sake, [perhaps] since they were slaughtered for their sake, they are not validated [by sprinkling] not for their sake? For in the chapter [entitled] HaTekhelet (Menachot 47b), the Talmud raises the dilemma: With regard to these sheep that one slaughtered for their sake and the bread was lost, what is the law as to whether we may sprinkle the blood of the sheep not for their sake, etc.? And if so, that which [the baraita] states, "the blood shall be sprinkled," deals [only] with [a case where] they were slaughtered not for their sake! And one must say: It is not comparable. For there, the sheep from the outset at the slaughter of the sacrifice — and the essence of the sacrifice — is validated through the bread; therefore, when the bread was lost, the sacrifice is found to be disqualified, and it is as though it were lost. But here, since an unspecified [sacrifice] is valid just like [one sacrificed] for its own sake, as [the Gemara] says at the beginning of Zevachim (2b), now too, even though he slaughtered them for their sake, for the sake of a remedy it is considered as though it were performed unspecified with regard to permitting the sprinkling of their blood. [If he slaughtered a burnt-offering or a peace-offering, that is indeed so according to Rabbi Akiva, as there is no loss]; rather, [we are dealing here with a case] where he slaughtered a sin-offering [first], for which there is no remedy of sprinkling [its blood] not for its sake, since a sin-offering is disqualified [when offered] not for its sake for the sake of voluntary peace-offerings, as a sin-offering cannot be brought voluntarily.

Tosafot on Nazir 28b:5:1.hebrew: דתנן אם גילח על אחת מהם יצא - כלומר, ולכך אמר ת"ק דכי נזרק אחד מן הדמים, אפילו חטאת דאיירי ביה ר"ע, דאינו מיפר — דמותר מיד לשתות יין, שהרי מגלח על אחת מהן, או חטאת או עולה או שלמים, וליכא ניוול. ולכך הוצרך לאיתויי ראיה לכך, [דלא תימא] דוקא גלח על השלמים הוא דתנן במתניתין "נזרק אחד מן הדמים", דדוקא מן השלמים יצא, דכתיב: "וגלח הנזיר פתח אהל מועד..."; וקאמר דבעל יצא על אחד משלשתן. ובפרק איזהו מקומן (זבחים דף נה.) מפרש לה, דמקיש חטאת, עולה ושלמים:
Tosafot on Nazir 28b:5:1.english: "As we learned: If he shaved after one of them, he has fulfilled [his obligation]" - That is to say, for this reason the first tanna said that once the blood of one of [the offerings] has been sprinkled — even [that of] the sin-offering, with which Rabbi Akiva was dealing — [the husband] cannot nullify [her vow], because she is immediately permitted to drink wine, since [a nazirite] shaves after [any] one of them, either the sin-offering, or the burnt-offering, or the peace-offering, and there is no [longer any] disfigurement. And therefore, [the Gemara] needed to bring a proof for this, [so that you should not say] that it was specifically [if one] shaved after the peace-offering that we learned in our Mishnah "the blood of one of them was sprinkled," [meaning] that specifically [if one shaved] after the peace-offering has he fulfilled [his obligation], as it is written: "And the nazirite shall shave at the door of the Tent of Meeting..." (Numbers 6:18); and [the Mishnah therefore] states that after the fact [bedi'avad] he has fulfilled [his obligation] upon [any] one of the three of them. And in the chapter [entitled] Eizehu Mekoman (Zevachim 55a), [the Gemara] explains it, that it juxtaposes the sin-offering, the burnt-offering, and the peace-offering.

Tosafot on Nazir 28b:7:1.hebrew: ה"ג איידי דזוהמא - בהם זוהמא, ואינו מגופה — מגני לבעל, ולא ניחא ליה:
Tosafot on Nazir 28b:7:1.english: This is the correct reading: "Since it is dirty" - [There is] dirt in them, and [the hair] is not from her body, [which] is repulsive to the husband, and he is not amenable [to it].

Tosafot on Nazir 28b:8:1.hebrew: האיש מדיר בנו בנזיר - שיאמר: "יהא בני נזיר", ויתחילו מנין הימים מיד, אפי' אין הבן יודע שאביו הדירו בנזיר. א"נ: דמדיר בנו בנזיר — שיצוה לבנו שיאמר: "הריני נזיר":
Tosafot on Nazir 28b:8:1.english: A man can vow that his son should be a nazirite - [This means] that he says: "Let my son be a nazirite," and the count of the days begins immediately, even if the son does not know that his father made him a nazirite. Alternatively, that "he vows his son as a nazirite" [means] that he commands his son to say: "I am hereby a nazirite."

Tosafot on Nazir 28b:8:2.hebrew: ואין האשה מדרת בנה בנזיר - כדמפרש בגמרא. "כיצד" — ל"ג:
Tosafot on Nazir 28b:8:2.english: "And a woman cannot vow that her son should be a nazirite" - As [the Gemara] explains in the Gemara. [As for the word] "How so?" — we do not read [it in the text].

Tosafot on Nazir 28b:8:3.hebrew: גילח או שגלחוהו - דאין לך מחאה גדולה מזאת. ולא מיבעיא גילח או שגלחוהו, אלא אפי' מיחה או שמיחו בדברים שאין רצונו שיעשה נזיר — מתבטל הנזירות. ובגמרא מפרש הטעמים. ודוקא כשמיחו מיד כששמעו; [אבל] אם לא מיחו, ושוב לימים מיחו — אין בכך כלום, אחרי שהתחיל הנזירות. ובתוספתא (פ"ג) קתני בהדי הני: "או שהביא ב' שערות". והא דלא תני במתני' — משום דשתי שערות מבטלות הנזירות אף אחר שהתחיל כבר למנות כמה ימים מנזיר, אבל הני דהכא דגילח ומיחה היינו בתחילת שמיעת הנזירות. ואפי' אם נאמר תגלחת ומחאה מבטלין [לאחר] שמיעה, אפי' [הכי] ניחא דלא תנא, דבפלוגתא לא קמיירי, דבגמ' פליגי בה רבי ור' יוסי בר' יהודה. א"נ, דלא קתני אלא מידי דביד אדם לבטל הנזירות:
Tosafot on Nazir 28b:8:3.english: [If] he shaved or they shaved him - For you have no greater protest than this. And it is not necessary [to state that if] he shaved or they shaved him [the naziriteship is canceled], but even if he protested or they protested in words, [saying] that he has no desire to become a nazirite, the naziriteship is canceled. And in the Gemara, [the Gemara] explains the reasons. And [this applies] specifically when they protested immediately upon hearing [of the father's vow]; [but] if they did not protest, and subsequently, days later, they protested, it is of no effect, since the naziriteship has already begun. And in the Tosefta (ch. 3), it teaches alongside these: "or if he grew two [pubic] hairs." And as for [the fact] that [our] Mishnah does not teach [this case of two hairs] — [it is] because two hairs cancel the naziriteship even after he has already begun counting several days of the naziriteship, whereas these [cases] here, of shaving and protesting, are at the initial hearing of the naziriteship. And even if we say that shaving and protest cancel [the naziriteship even] after hearing [it], even so it is well that [the Mishnah] did not teach [it], because it does not deal with a matter of dispute, for in the Gemara, Rabbi and Rabbi Yose, son of Rabbi Yehuda, disagree about it. Alternatively, [the Mishnah] teaches only something that is in human hands to cancel the naziriteship.

Tosafot on Nazir 28b:9:1.english: "If he had an animal separated" - As [explained] above.
